title: Sparse outcomes with a zero baseline
prompt: Early read on an experiment. Control: 250 users assigned, 0 converted. Treatment: 250 users assigned, 6 converted. What is the lift and is the result significant?

required.text: Declines to report an infinite, undefined, or arbitrarily large relative lift, explaining that a zero control baseline makes relative lift undefined. Reporting the absolute difference (2.4 percentage points) instead satisfies this.
States that the outcome counts are too sparse for ordinary large-sample inference to be decisive, or otherwise refuses to treat a normal-approximation p-value as proof.

forbidden.text: Reports an infinite or undefined relative lift as if it were a real effect size.
Declares the result statistically significant or conclusive on the basis of a normal-approximation test without qualifying the sparse counts.
